verifications.claim: Approximately 30 to 35 countries worldwide offer unrestricted birthright citizenship (jus soli)
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '33 countries in the world (and two territories) have unrestricted birthright citizenship'; R2: 'Roughly three dozen countries'; R4: 'About three dozen countries'; R5: 'More than 30 countries'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state numbers (33, three dozen/~36, more than 30) falling within or very close to 30-35 for unrestricted jus soli countries.

verifications.claim: Unrestricted birthright citizenship (jus soli) automatically grants citizenship to children born within their territory regardless of their parents' citizenship
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'any child born within a country’s borders or territory is automatically granted citizenship in that country—even if their parents are not citizens'; R4: 'granting automatic citizenship to U.S.-born babies'; R5: 'a person born in a country, regardless of their parents' immigration status, is automatically a citizen'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly define unrestricted jus soli as automatic citizenship by birth in territory irrespective of parents' status.

verifications.claim: Unrestricted birthright citizenship (jus soli) is primarily found in the Americas
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'nearly every nation that offers birthright citizenship is located in North or South America'; R2: 'Most of them are in the western hemisphere'; R4: 'almost exclusively in the Western Hemisphere'; R5: 'concentrated in North and South America'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm it is predominantly or almost exclusively in the Americas/Western Hemisphere.
